newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - June 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - June 26.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- Today's paper devotes five pages to stories related to Hong Kong's return to mainland rule.

- A frontpage story reviews how the Preliminary Working Committee of the Preparatory Committee for the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR), the Preparatory Committee for the HKSAR and Selection Committee Panel worked effectively together to guarantee a smooth transition.
- The 11th of a series of features on Hong Kong focuses on the territory's booming tourism.
- A full page is deveoted to stories calling for worldwide efforts to crack down on drug production, smuggling and abuse on the occasion of the International Day Against Drug Abuse.
FINANCIAL NEWS
- The Bank of China starts to issue financial news on a website on the Internet.
- Hong Hu, vice-minister of the State Commission for Economic Restructuring, says companies selected to be restructured into big company groups must establish a share-holding system.
- The Agricultural Bank of China sets up a committee to check and supervise financial risk.
- The China Agricultural Development Bank opens a telephone line for people to report on irregularities.
CHINA SECURITIES

- Chen Qingtai, vice-minister of the State Economic and Trade Commission, says the government should give preferential treatment in areas such as stock and bond issues to firms selected to be restructured into big company groups.
ECONOMIC DAILY
- Chinese officials say they will maintain production in the Guangzhou Peugeot car factory even if there is no new foreign partner.
- Gross output of China's silk industry hit 2.934 billion yuan in January-March, down by a year-on-year 11.24 percent.
ECONOMIC INFORMATION DAILY
- China's coal industry faces rising stockpiles as output by township mines surges.
CHINA BUSINESS DAILY
- The State Planning Commission is planning measures to curb salary rises and strengthen collection of personal income taxes.
- The Ministry of Internal Trade says China's trade volume with Hong Kong will further expand after the July 1 handover.
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH

- A frontpage story titled "Sincerely Safeguarding Hong Kong People's Interests" tells how central government has safeguarded Hong Kong people's interest with sincerity in past 13 years of transitional period.
- Leading officials from many countries believe that the return of Hong Kong to its motherland is of historical importance and express their warm congratulations.
CHINA DAILY

- Premier Li Peng expresses the hope that China and Russia will make joint efforts to push forward their good-neighborly relations. Li made the remark during a meeting with visiting Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov.
